Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting

Updated: October 23, 2026 21:30 Xinhua [![](/static/2023GW/images/Artical_Print.jpg)](javascript:window.print\(\))

BEIJING, Oct. 23 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday presided over a State Council executive meeting that studied measures to coordinate population development with economic and social development and heard a report on the implementation of the arrangements made at the national conference on the services sector.

Noting that population is fundamental to a country's economic and social development, the meeting called for efforts to tap the demographic dividend and support high-quality economic and social development through high-quality population development.

The meeting stressed the need to expand skills training and better align education and training with industrial development to promote high-quality and full employment.

It also called for steady progress in ensuring equal access to basic public services and optimizing the infrastructure layout in line with population distribution.

Efforts should be made to accelerate the development of a birth-friendly society and to maintain a stable number of newborns, according to the meeting.

Regarding the service industry, the meeting emphasized its underpinning role in driving economic growth and called for stronger support in areas such as financing, land use, talent and data.

The meeting urged continuous efforts to break down market access barriers, remove hidden hurdles for private investment, and explore innovative development paths tailored to local conditions.

It also emphasized the need to increase investment in the services sector to unleash the potential of service consumption as well as cultivate leading enterprises and distinctive brands.

China issues revised administrative measures for outbound investment

Updated: October 22, 2026 21:56 Xinhua [![](/static/2023GW/images/Artical_Print.jpg)](javascript:window.print\(\))

BEIJING, Oct. 22 -- China on Thursday unveiled revised administrative measures for outbound investment, aiming to provide stronger institutional safeguards for its development and security.

The measures, released by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), China's top economic planner, will take effect on Dec. 1, 2026, replacing the existing rules enacted in 2017.

The revision comes amid rapid growth in China's outbound investment and rising risks in an increasingly complex global environment, a spokesperson for the NDRC said.

The revised measures further affirm the principal role of various investors in outbound investment, including domestic enterprises, individual residents, and other organizations.

They also improve reporting systems for major adverse events and large overseas reinvestment projects, aiming to better protect the rights and interests of outbound investors and help them manage overseas risks.

The revision is part of the country's broader efforts to promote the high-quality development of outbound investment. In June, China issued a new regulation on outbound investment, which calls for proactively aligning with high-standard international economic and trade rules, advancing high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and promoting international cooperation in industrial and supply chains.

China's outbound investment has continued to expand in recent years. By the end of 2025, the country's outbound investment stock had reached nearly 3.4 trillion U.S. dollars, keeping China among the world's top three investors for nine consecutive years, according to the Ministry of Commerce.

The ministry also reported that China's outbound direct investment maintained steady and orderly growth, totaling 128.62 billion U.S. dollars in the first three quarters of 2026.

China unveils five-year plan to strengthen industrial foundation, upgrade manufacturing

Updated: October 22, 2026 17:26 Xinhua [![](/static/2023GW/images/Artical_Print.jpg)](javascript:window.print\(\))

BEIJING, Oct. 22 -- China on Thursday released a five-year plan to accelerate upgrading of its industrial foundation capabilities, in a further step toward building an innovation-driven manufacturing powerhouse.

The document, jointly issued by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and other government departments, calls for integrated efforts in technological breakthroughs and their application, addressing weaknesses in China's industrial foundation systematically, and achieving a comprehensive upgrade toward stronger innovation, greater self-reliance and higher quality.

Industrial foundation, the bedrock of manufacturing competitiveness, covers a range of areas including core components, basic materials and foundational software, as well as related talents, market conditions and the policy environment.

While China has built the world's largest and most complete industrial system over the past decades, its industrial foundation remains a weak link, experts said.

"The most critical issue is that China's industrial foundation is large but not strong," said Zhou Ji, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. He pointed to a structural imbalance, namely an oversupply of low-end products alongside a shortage of high-end ones.

Vulnerabilities and risks persist particularly in areas like integrated circuits and industrial software, Zhou noted.

As China pursues high-quality economic development and advances its new industrialization drive, the strengthening and upgrading of its industrial foundation has become increasingly critical.

According to the plan issued on Thursday, the weaknesses in China's industrial foundation will be significantly alleviated by 2030, while China's overall industrial foundation capabilities will reach internationally advanced levels, thereby providing strong support for building a modern industrial system anchored in advanced manufacturing.

A new cohort of single-champion manufacturers and "little giant" specialized enterprises in the industrial foundation sector should also be cultivated by then, the plan says.
